testcase.name: G1 to G5, G7, G9 and the phase-1 decisions hold for 3,000 random scenarios with binding budgets
G10: non-ambient effects never consume the placement reserve, however much they want
G9: a saturated viewer does not hold back the others; k grows until the next unit of cost exceeds the budget
G10 counterexample 2 (R2): placement cost is per viewer, so ambient may realize less than min(reserve, demand)
G10 counterexample 1 (R2): generation reservations are indivisible, so ambient may realize less than min(reserve, demand)
G3: the global, world and viewer budgets bind exactly; one viewer shared by three worlds is limited across worlds
Input order is irrelevant: shuffling the request list permutes the deliveries and changes nothing else
